note: The bombardier became incapacitated at 35,000 ft. The navigator did not fly because of a cold.

The pilot had severe gas pains. The summary describes hypothetical mission interference if the pilot had needed to go above 35,000 ft.
The summary records no mission interference by bends. A crew member reported dizziness treated with supplemental oxygen.
The summary describes severe non-incapacitating bends in the pilot, tail gunner and engineer.
The participants who ascended had no symptoms reported. Three listed pilots did not ascend.
The co-pilot had incapacitating bends. The navigator and bombardier had severe bends without incapacity.
The co-pilot was reported incapacitated by chokes.

The mission was reported completed. The log records a shoulder pain complaint and an individual who did not ascend.

The summary reports no mission interference. Some listed crew members did not ascend due to colds.
The summary reports no mission interference. The log describes a crew member feeling unwell and later looking sleepy.
Demand mask or regulator failure interfered with the mission. The summary explicitly attributes the interference to the equipment.
Joint pain and itching were recorded. The summary reports no mission interference.
A crew member with gas pains descended and returned after the symptoms resolved. The summary reports no mission interference.
An engineer gunner with increasing left-knee pain was reported incapacitated and descended in the air-lock.
The summary reports no mission interference. The log describes mild right wrist and arm pain.
The summary reports no mission interference. Several symptoms, including a leg cramp, are in the detailed log.
The bombardier was incapacitated. The author excludes bends as the cause and leaves the cause unknown.
The bombardier and assistant radio operator were reported incapacitated. The log records severe knee and chest pain and chokes in the detailed findings.
The summary reports no mission interference. The post-run examination reports a ruptured eardrum of uncertain onset.

The pilot was reported incapacitated by bends and descended in the air-lock.
The navigator had severe bends without incapacitation in the summary.
A sergeant had severe bends and was reported incapacitated. The log includes severe chest pain and descent in the air-lock.
The summary reports no mission interference. The log records coughing and a thumb-joint ache.

The summary reports no mission interference. The log documents pain resolving during descent and emergency oxygen use.
The navigator was reported incapacitated, and the pilot continued despite severe bends.
The summary reports no mission interference. An engineer had hand tremor.
The summary describes severe bends without radio operator incapacity. The log also describes a crew member descending and feeling better.
The co-pilot and engineer were reported incapacitated. The navigator's footnote links runs 55, 57 and 62.
The short mission was reported completed. The footnote links the same navigator across runs 55, 57, 62 and 63.
The summary reports oxygen apparatus difficulties and continuation of the mission without severe bends.
